title: Senate ethics panel to Bato dela Rosa: Respond to prolonged absence complaint
summary: The Senate committee on ethics and privileges has transmitted to Senator Ronald "Bato" dela Rosa the complaint lodged against him due to his prolonged absence.

blocks.text: The Senate committee on ethics and privileges has transmitted to Senator Ronald "Bato" dela Rosa the complaint lodged against him due to his prolonged absence.

The Wag Kang KuCorrupt group on Friday posted the panel's transmittal letter to Dela Rosa on Facebook. Committee chair Senator Tito Sotto, who signed the document dated October 22, 2026, later confirmed the complaint to reporters.

"This is to inform you of the action taken by the Senate Committee on Ethics and Privileges… on the complaint filed by Wag Kang KuCorrupt, represented by Barry Gutierrez, Cielo Magno, et al., against you for alleged prolonged absence from official duties," the document read.
The ethics panel gave Dela Rosa 15 days upon receipt of the complaint to provide his written response and any information regarding the matter.
Dela Rosa started missing Senate engagements in 2025 following reports that the International Criminal Court (ICC) had issued an arrest warrant against him.

He resurfaced on May 11, but left Senate custody in the early morning of May 14 after a shooting incident erupted inside the legislative chamber's premises. He has not been seen publicly ever since, and now faces a P50-million bounty for information leading to his arrest.

According to the transmittal, Wag Kang KuCorrupt's initial complaint was filed as early as February 25, but it was returned after the panel found it did not comply with rules. Supplemental affidavits to support the complaint were later submitted on September 14.
The panel then deemed the complaint "in substantial compliance, both in form and in substance" during an executive session on October 22, the same date of the letter.

"You (Dela Rosa) are invited to provide the Committee with any information relevant to the complaint, including a written response, within 15 days from receipt of this notice. A copy of the complaint, the Supplemental Affidavits, and the Rules is attached for your reference," the document read.
The group's petition reasoned that Dela Rosa's prolonged absence showed a dereliction of duty and a grave abuse of privilege.

"Under ordinary working conditions in both the public and private sectors, employees who fail to report for work without authorized leave are ordinarily subjected to disciplinary measures, including salary deductions, suspension, or even outright termination. Breadwinners across the country work tirelessly, often under difficult conditions, precisely because their families' welfare depends on daily accountability and performance," the group's original complaint read. — VDV, GMA News
